name: libirecovery
desc: Library and utility to talk to iBoot/iBSS via USB
why: Talks to Apple devices in recovery mode over raw USB, a door into iBoot and DFU low-level behaviour.

brief.what_it_is: libirecovery is a cross-platform C library and command-line tool that talks to iBoot/iBSS on Apple iOS devices over USB. The bundled utility is named irecovery, and its documented entry point is irecovery --shell, which opens an interactive shell on a device in recovery mode. From that shell you can run iBoot commands such as setenv and saveenv, or reboot the device. Input is a device attached over USB in recovery mode; output is terminal text and the library's API for other programs.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it is a fork of an older version from openjailbreak.org and is meant to be used with idevicerestore from the libimobiledevice project. The libimobiledevice homepage frames the wider effort as bringing Linux users access to iPhones, which were originally unavailable on that platform.
brief.how_it_works: It implements the USB communication to iBoot/iBSS, the low-level bootloader code that runs when a device is in recovery mode, rather than talking to services on a booted OS. It depends on libimobiledevice-glue and uses libusb on Linux and an IOKit USB backend on macOS, as shown in the configure output in the README.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew is the common route on macOS (the README gives brew install for build prerequisites, and the brief's brew package provides the binary). Building from source needs a C compiler, autotools (autoconf, automake, libtool), pkg-config, and libimobiledevice-glue. On Linux the README lists apt packages including libimobiledevice-glue-dev, libreadline-dev and libusb-1.0-0-dev, and says to run sudo ldconfig after install. On Windows the official route is MSYS2 with the MinGW 64-bit shell and its pacman packages. If PKG_CONFIG_PATH is needed, the README suggests export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/usr/local/lib/pkgconfig. To get a device into recovery mode, the README suggests the ideviceenterrecovery tool from libimobiledevice.
brief.standout: It reaches below the operating system: where libimobiledevice talks to services on a booted iPhone, this talks to the bootloader over raw USB, so it works when the device is in recovery mode and gives direct access to iBoot environment variables. That low-level access is what makes it useful for recovery and restore work.
brief.status: Maintained. The libimobiledevice homepage lists libirecovery 1.3.1 released 2025-10-17, with a news item for it on Oct 17, 2025, and the project's recent news items date to late October 2025. The README was last updated 2025-09-10. The homepage says the wider project has been in development since 2007.
brief.caveats: Needs a device in recovery mode, and the README tells users to make sure the device is not in normal mode before connecting. Windows requires MSYS2 for the official build route. Building from source needs several dependencies, and libimobiledevice-glue must be present first. The license is LGPL-2.1. The README states the project is independent and not approved by Apple. The README's build example still shows version 1.2.0 in its configure output, which is a minor documentation lag behind the 1.3.1 release. The homepage was unreachable for libirecovery specifics, so it describes the wider libimobiledevice project, and the release details come from its download section. The README's tone is simple and brief; it does not spell out risks of writing to iBoot variables.
quotes: The libirecovery library allows communication with iBoot/iBSS of iOS devices via USB.
libirecovery is a cross-platform library which implements communication to iBoot/iBSS found on Apple's iOS devices via USB. A command-line utility named `irecovery` is also provided.
This project is an independent software library and has not been authorized, sponsored, or otherwise approved by Apple Inc.
